head: e9e35067fc3b419a54d790a71663071455f203f1
changes: Trusted-cap CPU verification explicitly records and normalizes AIR/lookups through bounded graph preparation, using CPU constants and preserving independent verification.

Recording, normalization and packing each admit cumulative requested storage with a 64 MiB ceiling. Returned lookup metadata has a separate 64 MiB retained-capacity/Arc census; graph coexistence is bounded by 192 MiB with default limits.
The degree-analysis graph is released before packing. Prepared lookup arrays, names and expression Arcs transfer into common metadata by ownership.
Metadata descriptors have a 256-instance ceiling, exact fallible vector allocation and stack degree scratch. Invalid caps and invalid limits reject before AIR graph preparation.
Parity tests compare native upstream metadata, lookup topology and proof verification. Quota, invalid-geometry, callback-panic recovery, ownership and tampering tests cover both lane configurations.
Two full-size finalizers preserve the archived registry and every arithmetic-stage operation count, with all 16 proving arithmetic stages on OpenCL and independent CPU proof verification.

qualification_attempts.reason: Invalid-cap fixture used an empty cap; the upstream cap constructor panicked before the verifier was reached.
qualification_attempts.correction: Use a one-root cap, which is constructible but has the wrong registered geometry.

limitations: Verifier graph quotas bound requested storage, not complete physical RSS or scheduler phases. AIR callback allocations, native proof containers, verification arithmetic scratch, allocator/driver overhead and cached-program overlaps still need enclosing reservations.

The 192 MiB graph workspace ceiling follows coexistence of retained unpacked lookups with the recording/normalization graph, or with packing scratch. Descriptor arrays and the supplied cap are separate from this graph bound.
CPU reference proving and the native proof verifier arithmetic remain CPU paths. The new preparation explicitly selects CPU constants and does not alter GPU proving-stage coverage.
No scheduler allowance was reduced from observed peaks. Ordinary pool admission rejects this qualification profile without complete lifetime phases.
The 3 GiB worker, 4 GiB aggregate host, 7 GiB managed GPU and 1 GiB allocation caps remain enforced. Isolated finalizer timings do not establish sustained transactions per hour or a performance gain.
Broader transaction workloads, nonempty-child full-size merges, larger blocks, sustained pool throughput, multiple GPUs and AMD/Metal qualification remain open.
